title: One row of coverage.parquet
description: place x indicator x time grain: the time range, the number of periods, the last value, a short sparkline series, and on the indicator's status_grain row the default status and trend from its status_method. Built by `npm run coverage:build` (src/coverage/), which imports the same status functions as the viewer (src/status/). The Matrix, the report builder and the Scorecard read only this file.

place_name.description: The place's name in the gazetteer index (its id when the index lacks it), so the Matrix needs no other file.

coll.description: The values collection the row was read from (`places`, `mr_eez`): which values file holds it.

place_coll.description: The place's home gazetteer collection (`noaa_nerrs`, `mr_eez`): the first of its collections in the gazetteer's layers.json order, else `coll` (a place the index does not list, or a build without the index). The viewer groups places by it. Optional: coverage built before 2026-10-20 has no such column.

t0.description: First period start (null for grain all).

t1.description: Last period start (null for grain all).

last_value.description: Continuous: the last period's value. Categorical: the last period's largest share.

last_class.description: Categorical: the class with the largest share in the last period.

status_method.description: Set on the status_grain row only.

status.description: Recent mean against the long-term record; statistical, not better or worse.

lt_sd.description: Long-term sample SD (iea-sd); null for other methods.

why.description: Why status is null on a status_grain row (e.g. 'record of 6 years, fewer than 10').

spark.description: JSON {"t0": first period start, "g": grain, "v": [value or null, ...]} for the last 40 calendar periods (consecutive from t0, null for a gap, 4 significant digits), only on the row a viewer shows for the cell (the status grain, else the next grain with a value); [] otherwise and for categorical indicators. Readers also accept the older [[period start, value], ...].
